clue.text: Model I love in play

indicators.note: in says the two letters sit inside the word for a play

parts.note: a play is a drama
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: An actor-model confesses her love while appearing on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a three-dimensional scale scene, a kind of model display.

clue.text: Tug overwhelmed by river in flood

indicators.note: overwhelmed by says the tug word is engulfed by the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
to lug is to tug or haul

explanation.surface: A tugboat is swamped by a river in spate.
explanation.definitionFit: A deluge is a great flood or downpour, a synonym.

clue.text: Magic Circle: sect must include foremost of conjurors

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: must include says the sect word takes a letter inside it

parts.note: a cult is a sect

indicators.note: foremost of says take the first letter of conjurors

explanation.surface: The Magic Circle, the conjurors' society, is told it must admit the leading magician.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magic Circle is a real London society of magicians, which hides that Magic is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Occult means relating to magic and supernatural powers.

clue.text: General mood in a newly-built rest home about parking

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go around the parking letter
newly-built says the letters of rest home are constructed afresh in another order

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: The general mood in a brand-new retirement home is about car parking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly-built' rearranges REST HOME to TMOSHERE; 'about' puts it around P.
explanation.definitionFit: An atmosphere is the prevailing mood or feeling of a place.

clue.text: Colour of bream at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of the fish are jumbled

explanation.surface: The colour of a bream fish swimming in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is a yellowish-orange colour, named after fossil resin.

clue.text: Miss opportunity to wrap up, heading off

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter of the phrase is removed

parts.note: to close out is to wrap up or conclude

explanation.surface: Someone misses their chance to finish things because they had to leave early.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose out is an idiom for missing a chance or failing to benefit.

clue.text: Help from worker after stop in LA

indicators.note: after places the worker word behind the rest
in says the stop word sits inside LA

parts.note: an end is a stop
a hand is a worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: Assistance from a worker following a stopover in Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend a hand is an idiom meaning to help.

clue.text: Damage statuette, knocking its top off

indicators.note: knocking its top off says the first letter is removed, the top in a down clue

parts.note: the Oscar is the Academy Award statuette

explanation.surface: Someone damages an award statuette by breaking off its head.
explanation.definitionFit: To scar is to mark or disfigure, a form of damage.

clue.text: Somehow impound E in place frequented by drug addicts

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are rearranged in some unspecified way

explanation.surface: Police seize ecstasy at a haunt of drug users.
explanation.walkthrough: E is also slang for the drug ecstasy, which suits the drugs surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An opium den was a place where people went to smoke the drug.

clue.text: Continuously move up bound by rope?

indicators.note: bound by says the reversed word is held inside the rope word

parts.note: a tether is a rope

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to go is to move

explanation.surface: A climber keeps moving up while tied on by a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Together can mean without a break, as in working for hours on end.

clue.text: Stand-in starts to learn off Cambridge University master

indicators.note: starts to says take the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: C is a standard abbreviation for Cambridge
M abbreviates master, as in MA

explanation.surface: A substitute teacher begins learning the ropes from a Cambridge don.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or cleric temporarily filling in for another, a substitute.

clue.text: Dressing, group before getting on

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
getting on means growing old, ageing

explanation.surface: A band dresses up before going on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying a bandage to a wound is dressing it, a medical sense.

clue.text: Current leader of group associated with masterful playing

indicators.note: leader of says take the first letter of the word group
playing says the letters of masterful are played about with, rearranged

explanation.surface: The current frontman of a band is praised for his virtuoso playing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a warm Atlantic ocean current flowing from the Gulf of Mexico.

clue.text: Leave out some heirloom I treasure

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An owner decides to leave out part of a cherished family heirloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave out and omit are direct synonyms meaning to exclude.

clue.text: Drink before riding about on a horse after bad trips tackling short run

indicators.note: after places the about and horse letters behind the rest
tackling says the jumbled trips grip the shortened run
bad says the letters of trips are spoilt, rearranged
short says the last letter of run is cut

parts.note: C abbreviates circa, about
up means mounted, on a horse, as in a jockey being up

explanation.surface: A rider on horseback after some awkward stumbles takes on a short run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' makes STIRP, which 'tackling' wraps round the 'short' run; a mounted jockey is said to be up, hence 'on a horse'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup cup is a drink offered to a rider already mounted before a hunt.

clue.text: Rural types look outside hotel for a herb

indicators.note: outside says the rural types go around the hotel letter

parts.note: peasants are country folk, rural types
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: Country people peer in from outside a hotel, seeking some herb.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the common name of Adonis, a flowering plant classed as a herb.

clue.text: See 20
Account accompanying amount of paper daughter got

parts.note: a quire is a set measure of paper, 24 or 25 sheets
D abbreviates daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: A daughter got hold of some stationery along with the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Acquired means obtained or gained, a synonym of got.

clue.text: 'Prince of Tyre', almost priceless bust

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters are broken up and rearranged
almost says the last letter of priceless is dropped

explanation.surface: A near-invaluable bust of a royal figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last S; 'bust' then rearranges PRICELES.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's play is titled Pericles, Prince of Tyre, naming its hero.

clue.text: Supporters of Queen captured by revolutionary chiefs

indicators.note: captured by says the Queen's letters are held inside the others

parts.note: Che Guevara is the crossword's stock revolutionary
leaders are chiefs
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Royalist supporters of the Queen are taken prisoner by rebel commanders.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerleaders lead the crowd's cheering, so they are supporters of a team.

clue.text: Verse, extremely short, by Australian soldier, perhaps unfinished

indicators.note: extremely says take the extreme letters, first and last, of short
unfinished says the final letter is cut off

parts.note: an Anzac is a soldier of the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps

explanation.surface: A brief poem written by an Australian soldier, perhaps left incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines forming a unit of a poem, a verse.

clue.text: A cocktail relaxed Bryan, and bubbly

indicators.note: bubbly says the letters fizz and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bryan unwinds with a cocktail and some champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relaxed' looks like the anagram signal, but its letters are part of the fodder; 'bubbly' does the job.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a classic cocktail of brandy, crème de cacao and cream.

clue.text: Section without lights learner driver avoided

indicators.note: avoided says the learner letter is left out

parts.note: unlit means without lights
L is the learner plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A section of road with no street lighting is shunned by a nervous learner driver.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a component part or section of a larger whole.

clue.text: To be good enough at sums, reps will need to be trained

indicators.note: need to be trained says these letters must be drilled into a new shape

explanation.surface: To be competent at arithmetic, sales reps must take training.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass muster is an idiom for reaching an acceptable standard.

clue.text: Separate in Croatian resort

definitions.meaning: to separate is to divide or break apart
a port city on Croatia's Dalmatian coast

explanation.surface: Someone splits up while on holiday in Croatia.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means divide, and it is also a Croatian coastal city popular with tourists.

clue.text: Girl found over in Hammersmith

indicators.note: over says the letters are turned over, read backwards
in says the letters lie inside the place name

explanation.surface: A girl is discovered in Hammersmith, a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Emma is a common female first name, as in the Jane Austen heroine.

clue.text: Character, kind one to emulate

parts.note: a role is a character in a play
a model is a kind or type, as of a car

explanation.surface: A person of kind character is held up as someone to copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A role model is a person whose behaviour others try to imitate.

clue.text: Member of the clergy in chapter, unidentified

parts.note: anon, short for anonymous, means unidentified

explanation.surface: An unnamed cleric sits in a cathedral chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: a cathedral chapter is the body of clergy to which this cleric belongs.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a cleric attached to a cathedral, a member of its chapter.

clue.text: Hopelessness of the French couple

parts.note: des is French for of the (plural)
a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: A French couple's hopelessness.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is the total loss of hope, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Best lines written about one with a horticultural skill

indicators.note: written about says the best and lines words are set around the other letters

parts.note: top means best
RY, railway, gives railway lines
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The finest verses ever written about a gardener with a special skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Topiary is the art of clipping shrubs into ornamental shapes, a gardening craft.
